chapter: Harlem, Redman's band and the Savoy
title: Steve Dunn, and start of the April 25 session
summary: Jackson names Steve Dunn as a lyrical trumpeter; the tape is paused and the interview resumes on April 25.

blocks.x: We lost so great many. And while we didn't talk about it, of course I just [ ] some few trumpet players because in the brass department -- I asked you about trombone players later, but if you can think of any that I haven't asked you about, you just --
Uh-huh. Well, Steve Dunn was a very good, beautiful trumpet player. He played like Joe Smith, you know. He was a very good trumpet player back there in those days. [PAUSE]
Uh-huh. This is Sunday -- what is this, Brother?

This is Sunday, April 25. This is a continuation of oral history of what most musicians consider -- Quentin Jackson -- the super sideman. Undoubtedly one of the most renowned sidemen in the history of jazz.
